correction.pre_check: requires BOTH sidecars, not either. That is the defect the review reported, and it closes every fixed state its probe drives.

An earlier check looked before the thing it was checking for had happened.
correction.by_identity_not_name: the race removes both sidecars and creates two new files with the SAME names, so the comparison is on device and inode
correction.no_cleanup: an artifact the race produced is reported and left. Removing it would be the post-hoc cleanup the allocation and the review exclude, and it would race another opener's own file.

reviewer_probe_replayed.result: all three cases now REFUSE: only-wal and only-shm at the pre-check with nothing created, and serving-close-after-guard at the post-check, naming that the store was released and that the files were left rather than removed

residual_reported.what: in the race, the refusal comes after SQLite has already made the files, so the open leaves two artifacts behind even though it refuses
residual_reported.why_it_cannot_be_closed_here: the check and the open are separate operations in this sqlite3 build, and the only atomic alternatives are immutable=1 (excluded), post-hoc cleanup (excluded) or a VFS this allocation does not reach
smallest_decisions_available: accept the race: it needs a serving process to release the store inside a single open, and the open refuses rather than answering
permit removal of artifacts this opener demonstrably created, identified by device and inode -- which would need the no-cleanup rule relaxed
require the consumer to read only while a writer is attached, which is the case the allocation names and the one that creates nothing at all
